name: Captio AI
oneLine: A live captioning app for deaf and hard of hearing people that captions, translates and summarises speech in the room, on iPhone and Android.

platforms.detail: On the App Store (also listed for Apple silicon Macs and Apple Vision) and on Google Play since October 2026.

deviceRequirements.detail: The App Store lists iOS 15.1 or later for iPhone.

roomCaptions.detail: Speech in the room appears as text while the person is still talking.

groupConversations.text: One phone: speaker labels, names, direction
groupConversations.detail: One phone captions the whole table and labels each speaker. On iPhone it can name people by their voice, and on iPhone 16 and later a wave shows which side a voice comes from. Shared folders let several people add recordings to one place; live captions are not joined across phones.

languages.detail: Captions and translation in 60+ languages, including speech that switches languages mid-sentence.

offline.detail: Live captions need internet. Without a connection it keeps recording and transcribes automatically when the phone is back online.

speakerLabels.text: Yes, live and saved; names by voice on iPhone
speakerLabels.detail: Separates speakers (Speaker 1, Speaker 2). On iPhone it can learn saved voices and show their names instead.

voiceNames.detail: Save someone's voice once (about 20 seconds of talking, or an audio file) and their name and emoji show on every line they say, live and in saved recordings, instead of "Speaker 2". Voiceprints are made on the iPhone and never uploaded. When someone new talks for a while, Captio AI asks who it is. Free plan: your own voice plus one other person; Plus: more people.

speakerDirection.detail: With the iPhone flat on the table, a wave grows at the edge of the captions on the side the voice comes from, in that speaker's colour, while new words appear. It uses the iPhone's spatial microphones (not AirPods or an external mic), works in Live Captions and Live Translator, is calculated on the phone, and is free.

translation.detail: Live translation next to the original captions, with a two-way mode where each person reads the other in their own language.

saveTranscripts.detail: Recordings are saved with their audio in a searchable library and synced to your account.

export.detail: Share a transcript or summary as text, a link, a PDF, an email, or a prompt for an AI chat.

fileUpload.detail: Upload audio or video and get a full transcript with speaker labels.

summaries.detail: Turns transcripts into summaries, key points, notes, to-dos and follow-up messages. Free plan: 3 summaries in total.

customWords.detail: Add names, medical terms or specialist words so they are recognised.

display.detail: Text size, background colour and contrast can be adjusted.

soundAlerts.text: Yes, sounds in the captions; alerts vibrate
soundAlerts.detail: Recognize Sounds (version 1.1.5, iPhone and iPad) writes sounds into the captions where they happen, like [doorbell rings], in Live Captions, Live Translator and uploaded files. A doorbell, knocking, a smoke alarm, a siren, a phone ringing or a baby crying makes the phone vibrate, with a notification when the screen is locked during a recording. It works while Captio AI is recording, not as an always-on alarm. Recognized on the phone; free; not on Android yet.

phoneCalls.detail: Made for in-person speech picked up by the microphone, not for captioning phone calls.

videoCalls.detail: It is not a video-call captioning service.

mediaOnDevice.detail: It does not caption audio playing on the phone, but it can transcribe a saved audio or video file.

signLanguage.detail: Captio AI works with speech and text only.

privacy.text: Cloud; audio not stored on its servers
privacy.detail: Speech is processed by third-party speech recognition after you agree. Audio is not stored on Captio AI's servers; content is never sold or used to train AI models.

account.detail: Sign in with Apple or Google to sync, or skip and use it on one phone.

availability.detail: Available on the App Store and Google Play; prices differ by country.

freePlan.detail: Free every day: 100 free credits a day for live captions or transcription, and 3 AI summaries in total.

price.detail: Captio AI Plus on the US App Store, October 2026. No free trial. Prices differ by country.

accessibilityFunding.detail: No government funding programme; see captioai.app/organizations for licences through an organisation.

strengths.text: Captions, live translation, file transcription and AI summaries in one app, in 60+ languages.
Works on both iPhone and Android, and keeps captioning with the iPhone screen locked.
On iPhone it can learn the voices of people you talk to and show their names in the captions.

limits.text: Live captions need an internet connection; offline it only records and transcribes later.
The free plan gives 100 free credits a day; more needs Captio AI Plus.
It does not caption phone or video calls, and has no sound alerts or sign language.

sources.title: Recognize Voices: Captions That Show Who Is Talking by Name
sources.label: Recognize voices (Captio AI)
quotes: Their name and emoji show on every line they say, live and in saved recordings.
Ask them first, then let them talk about anything. It stops by itself once it has 20 seconds of speech.
Each voiceprint is made on your iPhone and stays there. It is never uploaded or synced.
When someone it doesn't know talks for a while, Captio AI asks who it is. One answer names them in every recording.
Names carry into exports and AI Summary, so the notes say who said what.
Yes. The free plan recognizes your own voice plus one other person. Captio AI Plus recognizes more people.

sources.title: Speaker Direction: See Where a Voice Is Coming From
sources.label: Speaker direction (Captio AI)
quotes: Put your iPhone 16 or later flat on the table and start Live Captions. Speaker direction is on by default.
A wave grows at the edge of the captions on the side the voice comes from, while new words appear.
The wave takes the colour of the talking speaker's tag, including the names you saved with Recognize Voices.
Works in Live Captions and in Live Translator sessions.
If you are on AirPods or an external microphone, captions stay on that microphone and the waves simply don't show.
Speaker direction is part of Live Captions, on the free plan and on Plus.
The direction is calculated on your iPhone from its microphones. It is not sent anywhere.

sources.title: Recognize Sounds: Doorbells and Alarms in Your Captions
sources.label: Recognize sounds (Captio AI)
quotes: On by default: doorbell, knocking, smoke or fire alarm, alarm or timer, siren, phone ringing, baby crying, dog barking, laughter, applause and music. Under More sounds you can add 17 more: car horn, cat, glass breaking, shouting, crying, door, water running, water boiling, microwave, beeping, whistling, singing, thunder, train horn, plane or helicopter, vacuum cleaner and coughing.
A doorbell shows where it rang, like [doorbell rings], in grey between the words, the way film subtitles do it.

The alert sounds: doorbell, knocking, smoke or fire alarm, alarm or timer, siren, phone ringing and a baby crying. The phone vibrates three times. If the screen is locked while you record, you also get a notification, for example "Doorbell".

No. Sounds are recognized while Live Captions or Live Translator are recording, including with the screen locked on iPhone, and in audio and video files you upload. It is not an always-on sound alarm.
Sounds are recognized on your iPhone or iPad. No audio is sent anywhere to do it.
Yes, free for everyone, on the free plan and on Plus. It comes with Captio AI version 1.1.5, on iPhone and iPad. It is not on Android yet.
